dishes.name: Andouillette de Troyes
dishes.desc: Pork sausage of strips of large intestine and stomach, seasoned and simmered for almost five hours, then grilled. The Aube's must-eat dish, from Troyes' butchery tradition.

dishes.name: Chaource
dishes.desc: Soft, mild cow's-milk cheese with a flowery rind, moulded by hand with ladles in the Aube village of Chaource. It has held AOC status for over 50 years.

dishes.name: Langres
dishes.desc: Cow's-milk cheese from Haute-Marne with a soft, creamy paste and a strong but not aggressive taste. A local cheese for the end of a meal.

dishes.name: Soumaintrain
dishes.desc: Raw cow's-milk washed-rind cheese from the Yonne, to be eaten well ripened. A farmhouse neighbour of Chaource and Saint-Florentin.

dishes.name: Champagne sauerkraut
dishes.desc: Sauerkraut from the plain around Brienne-le-Château, cooked with champagne and served with pork. The Aube is France's second-largest sauerkraut producer.
